seo.description: Explore Essaouira’s UNESCO medina: whitewashed lanes, blue shutters, sea walls and how to walk from Bab Marrakech to the Skala without the crowds.

name: Medina & Ramparts
hero_subtitle: White walls, blue doors and Atlantic light inside Morocco’s most walkable UNESCO coastal medina.

overview.title: A medina built for the wind
overview.p1: Essaouira’s medina was laid out in the 18th century with unusually straight streets for a Moroccan old town. White façades, blue woodwork and the constant Atlantic breeze define the mood.
overview.p2: Walk from the main gates toward the Skala, cut through the spice and thuya alleys, and keep returning to the sea walls whenever you want horizon and air.
overview.p3: It is compact enough for a first visit in half a day, rich enough for slow evenings after the day-trippers leave.

food.title: Food near the Medina
food.p1: Plan meals in medina squares, near the port for fish, or on the beach strip when you want ocean air.
food.li1: Grilled fish at the fishing port.
food.li2: Simple tagines in quieter medina restaurants.
food.li3: Café terraces on the main lanes.

1.title: Access

q1.question: Is the medina free?
q1.answer: Yes. Walking the streets and most rampart sections is free.

q2.question: How long do I need?
q2.answer: Two to four hours for a first loop including the Skala.

q3.question: Is it good with children?
q3.answer: Yes — mostly flat, but hold hands near the sea-wall drops.

q4.question: Best photo spots?
q4.answer: Skala de la Ville, blue door lanes and the port entrance.

q5.question: Crowded?
q5.answer: Main streets yes at midday in season; early morning is calmer.
